detection_candidates.rationale: medium — Windows Run-key writes are observable via registry-modification telemetry (Sysmon EID 13 / autoruns baselining); the Android BOOT_COMPLETED equivalent needs mobile EDR
medium — enumeration of installed AV/EDR products (service/registry/process queries) is observable in command-line and API telemetry on Windows, but is common and needs correlation
medium — process enumeration on Windows is observable via command-line/API telemetry but is common and low-fidelity in isolation
medium — outbound HTTPS to the specific C2 domains/IPs is detectable at the network egress (DNS/proxy/firewall) if those indicators are deployed, though the payload is TLS-encrypted
medium — the encrypted channel itself blends with normal TLS, but the specific C2 certificate/SNI and destination can be flagged via TLS-metadata and certificate-transparency-informed detections
medium — TLS/HTTPS to an unusual port (2053) is a detectable anomaly at the network egress via firewall/NetFlow analytics
medium — activation callbacks and any secondary payload retrieval are observable as anomalous outbound connections at network egress, but content is encrypted
medium — exfil rides the C2 channel; detectable via outbound-volume anomalies to the known C2 destinations at network egress, but encrypted
